project.name: Fast-print denture base resin
project.concept_label: Concept: project workspace for Claude Science (unofficial)
project.synthetic_label: Synthetic data · stress haystack (50 trials, eval only)

objective.label: Viscosity ≤ 1.5 Pa·s
objective.why: Thinner resin recoats faster between layers, so dentures print faster.

guardrails.label: 3-pt bend
guardrails.source_note: Modeled on ISO 20795-1 denture-base values; verify before quoting.

guardrails.label: Bubbles (porosity)
guardrails.plain: Few bubbles in the cured part

guardrails.label: Cytotoxicity
guardrails.plain: Safe for cells: at least 70% survive

stations.label: Weigh
stations.card: Weigh base monomer, diluent and photoinitiator into a 50 g batch. The balance logs each addition, so the recipe is recorded as weighed, not as planned.

stations.label: Mix
stations.card: Mix at 3000 rpm for 2 minutes, per SOP v1. The mixer logs speed, duration and when the run ended.

stations.label: Degas
stations.card: Pull a vacuum on the mixed resin so trapped bubbles expand and escape. Not in SOP v1, and the degasser has no data interface, so it's only logged if someone writes it on their worksheet.

stations.label: Viscosity
stations.card: Measure viscosity at 25 °C. This is the objective: at most 1.5 Pa·s.

stations.label: Print
stations.card: Print 6 tensile dogbones and 3 bend bars. The printer logs when each job starts, which is how the rest time between mixing and printing is known.

stations.label: Post-cure
stations.card: Post-cure under UV at 60 °C for 45 minutes. The oven has no interface, so the time is entered by hand.

stations.label: Test
stations.card: Pull and bend the printed parts, image a cross-section for bubbles, and run the cell-viability assay. Results land in the log automatically.

ledger.text: Campaign C (Dana Whitfield): 2 trials at 20–26% diluent; 2 passed every guardrail; viscosity 1.9–2.27 Pa·s.
Post-cure for 30 min reaches full strength; going to 45 min adds nothing.
Campaign M (Tomás Herrera): 6 trials at 19–30% diluent; 5 passed every guardrail; viscosity 1.62–2.36 Pa·s.
Corrects L2: matched recipes post-cured 45 min are stronger in tension than at 30 min. Use 45 min, as in SOP v1.
Campaign A (Cooper Shea): 6 trials at 16–24% diluent; 6 passed every guardrail; viscosity 1.93–2.49 Pa·s.
Campaign F (Ravi Menon): 6 trials at 28–34% diluent; 1 passed every guardrail; viscosity 1.39–1.7 Pa·s.
Campaign B (Cooper Shea): 2 trials at 35–36% diluent; 1 passed every guardrail; viscosity 1.35–1.36 Pa·s.
Dead end: high diluent (> 30%) too brittle.
ledger.status_note: Porous with brittle fracture in 1 of 1 included campaign-B trials.

ledger.text: Campaign H (Ravi Menon): 2 trials at 34–35% diluent; 1 passed every guardrail; viscosity 1.32–1.38 Pa·s.
Campaign N (Tomás Herrera): 4 trials at 27–33% diluent; 0 passed every guardrail; viscosity 1.36–1.7 Pa·s.
Campaign E (Dana Whitford): 4 trials at 40–45% diluent; 1 passed every guardrail; viscosity 1.02–1.15 Pa·s.
Why did porosity jump this winter? Same recipes as the autumn.
Campaign D (Dana Whitfield): 5 trials at 27–34% diluent; 0 passed every guardrail; viscosity 1.42–1.74 Pa·s.
Campaign K (Lucia Ferreira): 6 trials at 29–35% diluent; 5 passed every guardrail; viscosity 1.38–1.66 Pa·s.
Campaign G (Greeshma): 2 trials at 32–34% diluent; 2 passed every guardrail; viscosity 1.4–1.5 Pa·s.
Campaign P (Ines Kowalski): 5 trials at 28–40% diluent; 5 passed every guardrail; viscosity 1.15–1.72 Pa·s.
Can we reach 1.5 Pa·s without new materials?
